_comment: Dependency ceilings declared by the mitmproxy release that proxy/Dockerfile builds FROM.
proxy/requirements.txt deliberately does not list mitmproxy — it ships in the base
image — so the resolver cannot see these ranges and will float transitives straight
past them. Every cap in that file exists to restate a bound from this table, and is
therefore NOT inferable from what the package has published. Dependabot has twice
proposed changes that contradict it (#108 pyOpenSSL, #115 typing-extensions).
tests/test_lock_consistency.py enforces this table in two directions: locked pins must
satisfy these constraints, and proxy/requirements.txt must not permit anything in
must_reject. Update this file only when proxy/Dockerfile's base image tag changes;
verify against PyPI metadata for the new mitmproxy version.
Verified against PyPI metadata for mitmproxy 12.3.1 on 2026-10-26.

cryptography.note: 50.0.2 is the newest release, so the lock currently sits on the ceiling.

pyopenssl.note: pyOpenSSL 26.3+ requires cryptography>=49, satisfiable since 12.3.0 raised the cryptography ceiling.

typing-extensions.note: Applies on python<3.13 only; the base image runs 3.14, where mitmproxy does not require it at all.

certifi.note: No upper bound declared by mitmproxy.

brotli.note: 12.3.1 pins the CVE-2026-111497 fix exactly; 12.3.0 capped it at the vulnerable 1.2.0.
